role_sought: Councillor of the Province of Rome (Alleanza Nazionale)
detail: Ran for Alleanza Nazionale after winning the party's primary for Rome's XI municipio; served as provincial councillor until 2002.
Candidate on the regional list of centre-right presidential candidate Francesco Storace, whose defeat meant the list's candidates did not win seats.
Elected at 29 from eighth place on AN's closed list; subsequently elected Vice-President of the Chamber (May 2006).

role_sought: Deputy, Lazio 2 constituency (Il Popolo della Libertà list)
detail: Re-elected on the PdL closed list; appointed Minister for Youth in the fourth Berlusconi government on 8 May 2008.
First election for the newly founded Fratelli d'Italia, part of the centre-right coalition; she became leader of the FdI group in the Chamber in the XVII legislature.

role_sought: Member of the European Parliament (FdI list leader in all constituencies)
detail: Fratelli d'Italia fell short of the 4% threshold and won no seats despite her preference votes.

role_sought: Mayor of Rome (FdI, Noi con Salvini and civic lists)
result: Lost in first round (third place); elected to the city council
detail: Finished third behind Raggi and Giachetti and did not reach the run-off; FdI's own list took 12.27%. She took a seat on Rome's city council.

role_sought: Deputy, single-member constituency Lazio 2 – 07 (Latina), centre-right coalition
detail: Won the Latina single-member seat; FdI nationally rose to 4.35%.

role_sought: Member of the European Parliament (FdI list leader in all constituencies)
detail: Elected in every constituency but renounced the European seat to keep her seat in the Chamber of Deputies.

role_sought: Deputy, single-member constituency Abruzzo – 03 (L'Aquila), centre-right coalition; FdI leader and coalition's de facto prime-ministerial candidate
vote_share: 51.49% in the constituency; FdI about 26% nationally
detail: FdI became the largest party in both chambers and the centre-right coalition won an absolute majority, leading to her appointment as Prime Minister on 22 October 2022.

role_sought: Member of the European Parliament (FdI list leader in all constituencies)
detail: As sitting Prime Minister she announced on 28 April 2024 that she would head FdI's lists and renounce the seat if elected, the office of MEP being incompatible with that of Prime Minister; FdI came first nationally.
